item.title: China's "Golden Week" sparks travel boom in Central Asia
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BUKHARA, Uzbekistan, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- As the setting sun cast a golden glow over the ancient streets of Bukhara, the historic city bustled with tourists, while local vendors called out to passersby. Holding a hand-painted ceramic bowl, Yan Hong, a tourist from northeast China's Harbin, marveled at the intricate floral patterns adorning the craft at a roadside stall, accompanied by her parents. "Uzbekistan has so many historic cities along the Silk Road: Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva," she said. "I'd read about them in books. I had to see them for myself." Walking through the ancient city, she said the experience surpassed her expectations, with history and modernity blending seamlessly and different civilizations engaging in a quiet dialogue. Yan is among a rapidly growing number of Chinese travelers choosing Uzbekistan as a holiday destination. A mutual visa-exemption agreement, which officially took effect on June 1, 2025, has given fresh impetus to cross-border tourism. According to official reports from Uzbekistan's Tourism Committee, the number of Chinese tourists visiting the country increased by 3.5 times following the launch of the reciprocal visa-free policy. "By now, the entire city of Bukhara knows that China enjoys a seven-day 'Golden Week' holiday in October," said Khamrayev, a local vendor specializing in miniature paintings and traditional handicrafts. Recalling the holiday period last year, Khamrayev said Chinese tourists had flocked to his courtyard shop, making it his busiest sales period of the year. A similar tourism boom is unfolding in neighboring Kazakhstan, which also benefits from a mutual visa-free arrangement with China. At Shymbulak resort near Almaty, with the towering Tianshan Mountains in the background, Qi Yue and his wife from Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, waited in line for a cable car. "We decided on a whim," Qi said. "Visa-free travel was a big factor." He added that many Chinese tourists now travel to Kazakhstan from Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region after exploring the region. Some travelers are taking advantage of improved cross-border access to embark on longer and multi-country journeys across Central Asia. Zhang Dongni, a solo backpacker traveling overland across the region, made her way from Almaty to Lake Issyk-Kul in Kyrgyzstan. She was heading to Osh, the country's second-largest city, before continuing to Khujand in Tajikistan. "People here are remarkably warm and hospitable," Zhang said. While traveling from Bishkek to Osh, she was unable to board a bus because of her oversized luggage, so she arranged to share a taxi with local residents. "We chatted using translation apps the whole way. When we arrived, they insisted on covering my fare as their guest," Zhang said. In return, she gave them traditional Chinese knots as tokens of appreciation. In Tashkent, Uzbekistan's capital, Chinese tourists Zhou Yushan and Tang Suyu stopped to take photos outside the Holy Assumption Cathedral. "We took three days off to bridge the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays," Zhou said. "That gave us enough time to explore Xinjiang alongside several destinations across Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan on a single trip." As China and Central Asian countries continue to facilitate cross-border travel, growing tourism flows are increasingly becoming a two-way exchange, with more visitors from Central Asia also traveling to China. According to data from the Guangzhou Baiyun exit-entry frontier inspection station, more than 90,000 passengers from the five Central Asian countries had passed through Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport by June 2 this year, up 286.6 percent year on year. Arrivals from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan rose by 258.4 percent, 351.9 percent and 660.6 percent, respectively. Linked by mountains and rivers and bound by longstanding cultural ties, China and Central Asian countries are seeing closer people-to-people exchanges as cross-border travel becomes more convenient, opening new avenues for mutual understanding and lasting friendship.■

item.title: World's highest bridge emerges as new tourism attraction
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
GUIYANG, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- Thousands of visitors flocked to the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge during China's recent week-long National Day holiday, not simply to cross the world's highest bridge in southwestern Guizhou Province, but to stop and explore the surrounding area. Built to cut a two-hour journey across the canyon to about two minutes, the bridge is now drawing travelers who come for the wonder itself, and for a growing mix of sightseeing, adventure sports, dining and nighttime experiences. Spanning the Huajiang Grand Canyon, the 2,890-meter-long bridge connects Bouyei-Miao autonomous county of Guanling with Zhenfeng County in Guizhou. In April 2026, the bridge was certified by Guinness World Records as the world's highest bridge, with a confirmed height of 626.01 meters. However, setting a record-breaking height was not a goal in itself. The Huajiang Grand Canyon runs east to west for about 80 kilometers and cuts directly across the route of the Liuzhi-Anlong Expressway, making a major crossing difficult to avoid. Yang Jian, chief engineer responsible for the bridge's design, said lowering the structure would have required longer tunnels through the mountains on either side, increasing overall construction costs and potentially adding to driver fatigue. The final route therefore struck a balance between the bridge and tunnels, and almost incidentally placed the bridge more than 600 meters above the river, Yang added. Integrating tourism into the project was part of the plan long before the first cars crossed the bridge. From the design stage, the bridge and more than 50 square kilometers of surrounding area were incorporated into an overall tourism plan. Rather than adding attractions after construction was completed, designers looked for ways to turn parts of the bridge into visitor spaces. A maintenance passage inside the steel truss was converted into a 796-meter sightseeing corridor. A glass observation hall and a platform for aerial sports were built near the center of the bridge, while structural elements originally designed to improve wind stability were adapted to support a 1,411-meter elevated running track. Visitors can take elevators into the bridge structure, walk along the sightseeing corridor and look out over the canyon from hundreds of meters above the river. Those seeking more thrills can try bungee jumping, a narrow-plank walk suspended over the canyon or running on the elevated track. At night, water screen and light shows offer a different view of the bridge. During the National Day holiday, concerts, racing activities and food events further broadened the range of experiences available to visitors. On the Zhenfeng County side, shuttle buses carry visitors to the bridge tower, where elevators lead directly to the sightseeing area inside the structure. Since the bridge-tourism project began operation, it has recorded about 3.3 million visits, according to the project operator. Cheng Guojian, who visited the bridge with his family from southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, said the bridge was a much-anticipated stop they had planned before setting out. He set aside a full day to visit the bridge and its sightseeing facilities. "If there were no bridge, we might still pass through this area, but we would not stop and spend so much time," Cheng said. Liang Yan, a visitor from Guiyang, also made a special trip to the bridge and chose to stay overnight nearby to see both the daytime scenery and the evening light and water screen shows. Some visitors have come from far beyond Guizhou. In May, Iseult Alice Fitzpatrick, an Irish student at Harvard University who was visiting China for the first time, chose an unusual way to see the bridge. Wearing a safety harness, she took on a narrow-plank walkway suspended high above the canyon, crossing from one side and then making her way back. An outdoor enthusiast who enjoys hiking and rock climbing, Fitzpatrick said she did not want to miss the chance to try something so unusual on the world's highest bridge. On her return, she stopped midway, more than 600 meters above the water, simply to take in the scenery. "It's a very fun way to view it, because you're by yourself. And you're really high up, and it feels like being very close with nature, and you're just looking down at it. It's an incredible view. It's like nothing I've ever seen before," she said. The growing tourism economy around the bridge offers another measure of its impact. Since the bridge opened to traffic, Huajiang Township and nearby areas have received more than 1.48 million visits, according to local officials. The township has added 124 food and beverage businesses and 15 hotels and guesthouses, while tourism-related growth has indirectly created jobs for more than 2,000 local residents. For fruit trader Huo Zhenggui, who has long done business in Huajiang Township, the bridge has shortened delivery times and brought more customers. "Before, the mountain roads were rough, and the journey was long. Transporting fruit took a lot of time and caused heavy losses," Huo said. "Now that the bridge is open, the fruit looks as fresh as if it has just been picked from the tree. There are more tourists, and business is better than before." Hotels have also benefited from the influx of visitors. "There used to be very few guesthouses in the town, and many houses stood empty for long periods," said Wu Fuying, manager of Xiyuan Hotel in Huajiang Township. "Now that the bridge is open, rooms are often fully booked on weekends and public holidays. Visitors are coming, and they are willing to stay." ■

item.title: Zheng reaches China Open final first time
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Zheng Qinwen hits a return during the women's singles semifinal between Zheng Qinwen of China and Elise Mertens of Belgium at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin) BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China's Zheng Qinwen defeated Belgium's Elise Mertens 7-5, 6-2 here on Saturday to reach the China Open women's singles final for the first time, while home veteran Zhang Shuai and the Czech Republic's Katerina Siniakova advanced to the women's doubles final. Zheng, a wild card, broke 13th seed Mertens in the second game, but the Belgian broke back in the seventh to level at 4-4. After a tight finish to the opening set, Zheng prevailed 7-5 before taking control of the second to seal the victory. The result marked Zheng's best performance at the event and made her the first home player in tournament history to reach the singles final. "The best version of me will come in the future," reflected Zheng right after the match. "I spare no effort here (China Open). I will give it all out and present a good match tomorrow." Zheng will face this year's French Open champion Mirra Andreeva in Sunday's final after the fourth seed cruised past the Czech Republic's Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 6-2 in the other semifinal. "I'm very happy and excited to be in the final," said Andreeva. "Obviously she (Zheng) is aggressive, she likes to hit a lot of balls, she tries to play fast. I will try to play my best in the final." In the women's doubles, top seeds Zhang and Siniakova defeated Indonesia's Aldila Sutjiadi and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe 6-4, 6-2 to reach the final. The women's singles and doubles finals are scheduled for Sunday. ■ Zheng Qinwen celebrates after the women's singles semifinal between Zheng Qinwen of China and Elise Mertens of Belgium at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 10, 2026. item.title: China warns against Japan's rising neo-militarism
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese defense spokesperson on Saturday warned that neo-militarism in Japan has become a "mutant gray rhino running out of control," posing a serious threat to the post-WWII international order, the international non-proliferation regime, and regional peace and stability. Chen Xi, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, made the remarks when asked to comment on Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's recent speech on Japan's defense capabilities and the latest discussions on a planned revision of the country's three national security documents. As a defeated country in World War II, Japan must fulfill its obligations in eradicating militarism and destroying war-making power, and is forbidden to be re-armed for war, Chen said. However, Chen said that the current Japanese administration is using "neighboring security threat" as an excuse to expedite remilitarization, and even attempt to breach the three non-nuclear principles and progressively ease nuclear restrictions. "By doing this, Japan is steering its security policy toward an offensive, expansive and dangerous track," he said. Japan should earnestly reflect on its war crimes, make a clean break with militarism, and cease its dangerous attempts at constitutional revision for military expansion and nuclear weapon possession, Chen noted. ■

item.title: Mainland slams Lai Ching-te's secessionist narrative
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Saturday criticized Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te for clinging to a secessionist mindset, provoking confrontation, and undermining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media question about Lai's speech delivered in Taipei earlier in the day. Lai's speech disregarded facts, distorted right and wrong, misled the public and harbored ulterior motives, Zhang said, describing it as a typical display of his self-proclaimed stance as a "pragmatic worker for Taiwan independence." In his speech, Lai played up the so-called mainland threat and promoted the false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism," Zhang said. Lai was attempting to pursue "Taiwan independence" through military buildup and reliance on external forces, the spokesperson added. The Taiwan question stems from a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, but the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. The one-China principle is a basic norm governing international relations, a prevailing consensus in the international community, and an integral part of the post-World War II international order, Zhang said. "The future of Taiwan must be decided jointly by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots," the spokesperson said. The mainland will uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, work with people from all sectors of society in Taiwan, resolutely combat secessionist forces, and oppose external interference, Zhang said. The mainland will also deepen cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, and promote the peaceful and integrated development of cross-Strait relations, she noted. ■

item.title: China to launch initiative to boost employment amid AI advances
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- In China's latest effort to adapt its workforce to rapid technological changes, a senior official on Saturday announced an initiative to promote employment in response to artificial intelligence (AI) development. Li Zhong, vice minister of human resources and social security, said at a press conference that China would actively address the impact of AI and other emerging technologies on employment, promoting the responsible development of technology and bolstering quality employment. Adapting to AI-driven changes has become an increasingly prominent part of China's employment policy. Several official documents issued this year have outlined measures to harness technological advances while supporting employment. The 2026 government work report vowed to take more effective measures to facilitate employment and entrepreneurship through better adaptation to the development of AI technologies. A five-year plan on implementing the employment-first strategy also identified promoting employment amid AI advances as a key task, calling for creating jobs through AI applications and tapping the potential in traditional sectors. AI is already reshaping China's economy and transforming its labor market, with demand growing for workers equipped with specialized technical skills. According to Maimai, a networking and recruitment platform, the number of new AI-related job postings in the new economy on the platform rose 789.47 percent year on year from January to July. Online job-seeking platform Zhaopin also said in a report that demand was particularly strong for AI engineers, including those working in automotive manufacturing and intelligent driving. China's core AI industry has exceeded 1.2 trillion yuan (about 178.23 billion U.S. dollars) in scale, with more than 6,200 enterprises operating in the sector. AI adoption rate across key industries has surpassed 80 percent. Beyond AI, China is also seeking to generate employment opportunities by developing emerging and future industries. During the past five years, China introduced 72 new occupations, including AI trainers and carbon emissions managers, incorporating them into the country's official occupational classification system. Since the beginning of 2026, authorities have announced another 11 new occupations. Wu Liduo, an official of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, said Saturday the ministry would establish a regular mechanism for identifying new occupations, focusing on emerging fields such as AI, the digital economy, green and low-carbon development, and modern services. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the ministry plans to formulate or revise more than 200 national occupational standards, Wu said. Amid the changes brought by technological advances, China's overall employment situation has remained stable. The country created 10.52 million new urban jobs in the first nine months of 2026, achieving 87.7 percent of its annual target, according to figures released at Saturday's press conference. The surveyed urban unemployment rate averaged 5.2 percent in the first eight months of the year. ■

item.title: China, EU reaffirm stable, balanced ties as key trading partners: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China and the European Union (EU) have reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining stable and balanced trade ties as key trading partners after a meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, an official with China's commerce ministry said Saturday. Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic jointly chaired the second meeting of the consultation mechanism from Thursday to Friday in Beijing. The two sides confirmed that they would address trade and economic differences and each other's concerns in a balanced manner within the framework of World Trade Organization (WTO) rules, explore ways to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and promote balanced growth and further development in China-EU trade. Both sides agreed the consultation mechanism had been operating smoothly and efficiently, and that "the successful convening of its second meeting marked a new beginning rather than an end," said the official. The outcomes agreed upon at the meeting demonstrated that China and the EU had both the willingness and the wisdom to manage and properly resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, effectively preventing tensions from escalating, the official said. The two sides held intensive consultations in a spirit of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, discussing in depth ways to address each other's concerns on an equal footing, expand two-way market access and promote dynamic balance in China-EU trade, covering topics including medical devices, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, inverters, and agri-food products. According to the official, the two sides agreed to explore the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain goods within the framework of WTO rules, and hold a technical dialogue on the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation. In-depth discussions were also held on trade in electric and hybrid vehicles, which helped prevent further escalation, effectively safeguarded the actual export interests of Chinese companies and supported the stable development of China-EU trade in hybrid vehicles. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to addressing each other's concerns regarding export controls. The EU side will continue to work toward making progress in resolving key licensing cases involving China in the dual-use sector, said the official. They agreed that China and the EU have significant potential for cooperation in new energy, artificial intelligence, trade in services, the digital economy, and green and low-carbon development, and that they could further explore new opportunities and expand areas of cooperation. China will continue to welcome EU companies investing and doing business in China and to improve its business environment, said the official. China also expects the EU to provide Chinese companies with a fair, transparent and predictable business environment, effectively protect their legitimate rights and interests, and strengthen their confidence and expectations regarding investment and business operations in the EU. Looking ahead, the two sides will step up efforts on key trade and economic issues of mutual concern and work together to implement the outcomes and agreements reached at the meeting, said the official. They also agreed to hold the third meeting of the mechanism in March 2027. In the meantime, they will maintain close communication at all levels, including through a ministerial-level video conference next January. It was agreed that stable and healthy China-EU economic and trade relations serve their shared interests and also inject certainty and positive momentum into global economic growth and the stability of industrial and supply chains, said the official. ■

item.title: 90 years on, Long March spirit endures in China, resonates beyond borders
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
*The Long March spirit highlights the firm faith, strong will, and never-give-up attitude of the whole Party and all Chinese people to overcome major challenges during the revolutionary years. *In today's environment, people need to hold fast to the same values that made the Long March an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history, said Khairy Tourk, professor of economics at the Stuart School of Business at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. *The Long March is not only a towering monument in the development of the Chinese nation, but also a precious spiritual asset for all humanity in the pursuit of independence, freedom and liberation, said Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist. BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. The arduous journey, which lasted from 1934 to 1936, helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Nearly a century later, the Long March remains an important window into China's history and development. "The Long March is like a spine of your body that goes right through the modern history of China," said Harold Weldon, an Australian publisher and filmmaker. For China watchers, understanding this pivotal chapter is essential to understanding the CPC's founding ideals and enduring mission, as well as the resilient spirit of the Chinese nation. GREAT TURNING POINT The victory of the Long March marked a great turning point for the CPC and the Chinese revolution, and stands as a towering monument in the historic process of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. During the epic military trek, the CPC-led Red Army broke through encirclement by Kuomintang forces. Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. "It was probably the greatest tale of human endurance in recorded history, I think, in terms of the hardships faced," said Weldon. The Long March is a classic example of the ability of the Chinese people to defy overwhelming odds, and is ready to put up with huge sacrifices in treasure and blood in order to achieve their goals, said Khairy Tourk, professor of economics at the Stuart School of Business at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago, noting that "sacrifice is an essential part of achieving glorious victories." Paul Ilado, editorial director of Kenya's Radio Africa Group, said the Long March transformed a military retreat into a decisive political and historical turning point. The Red Army was under enormous pressure, he noted, and their ability to survive the encirclement campaign was crucial to the continuation of the movement. The historical significance of the Long March extends beyond military survival, Ilado said. As part of the CPC's revolutional legacy, he said, the Long March demonstrated that hardship had to be overcome, objectives pursued over the long term, and survival under extreme pressure sustained by organization and discipline. During the Long March, Red Army officers and soldiers were pushed to the extremes of their physical limits, turning this dramatic episode in world military history into a "glorious human miracle." The Long March spirit highlights the firm faith, strong will, and never-give-up attitude of the whole Party and all Chinese people to overcome major challenges during the revolutionary years. Wagner Lacerda Dantas, a Brazilian journalist with China International Communications Group, described the spirit as the determination to continue fighting for a collective goal even when circumstances appear almost impossible, bringing together conviction, courage, discipline, solidarity, sacrifice and confidence in victory. "What impressed me the most was the organizational cohesion and belief of the Red Army, although under extremely tough conditions," said Balew Demissie, senior consultant at the Policy Studies Institute of Ethiopia. When facing extreme natural environments such as snow-capped mountains and marshlands, as well as the chasing and interception by the enemy's materially superior forces, this army did not collapse, but instead demonstrated astonishing discipline and idealism, and ultimately achieved success, he added. Yuri Tavrovsky, head of the Expert Council of the Russian-Chinese Committee for Friendship, Peace and Development, likewise identifies endurance, sacrifice, patriotism and wisdom as qualities forged during the Long March. In his view, the experience helped shape a generation of leaders capable of confronting crises, assessing changing circumstances and finding a way forward. CONTEMPORARY ECHO The Long March belongs to a specific historical period, and China's circumstances today are vastly different from those of the 1930s, but foreign observers see its enduring relevance in the CPC's strong leadership and China's rapid development. In today's environment, people need to hold fast to the same values that made the Long March an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history, said Tourk, the economics professor at the Illinois Institute of Technology. "Without values such as sacrifice, patriotism, perseverance, and firmness, the people would lose their sense of direction," he said. "I believe that understanding the Long March is truly one of the best ways to understand how the Communist Party of China managed to grow under such adverse circumstances," said Dantas, the Brazilian journalist, adding that it demonstrated characteristics such as discipline, unity, organizational capacity, independence and autonomy, seeking truth from facts, and, above all, confidence in the masses. "The great strength of the Party during that period lay not only in its weapons, but in its ability to maintain close ties with the people," he said. Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist, said that amid life-and-death trials, Chinese Communists demonstrated unshakable ideals and convictions and made strategic choices decisive for the future of the Chinese revolution. "For China today, it remains a powerful source of motivation that encourages the people to overcome difficulties, advance Chinese modernization, and realize the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he added. During a visit to China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Ilado, the editorial director of Kenya's Radio Africa Group, was struck by the transformation of land that had once been difficult to cultivate, which offered him a tangible way to think about the legacy of the Long March. "When I arrived in China and went to Ningxia, I was amazed at how a desert had been turned into productive land, and how today that area has become a breadbasket for the country and the world," he said. The connection, Ilado stressed, is the idea of undertaking a difficult journey over a long period without losing sight of the destination. A farmer cultivating difficult land, an engineer building irrigation infrastructure, a technician improving food processing or a young person leaving a poor rural community to pursue education may seem far removed from the Red Army of the 1930s, yet all can be understood through the determination to continue when the destination is still far away, Ilado noted. Joshua Kingdom, a research fellow at Uganda's Development Watch Center, sees the Long March spirit reflected in China's response to contemporary challenges. He said China's efforts to withstand external pressure demonstrated resilience and a determination to deepen cooperation with Global South economies rather than succumb to difficulties. BEYOND CHINA The significance of the Long March extends beyond the history of China. The Long March spirit of unwavering faith, perseverance and collective spirit transcends borders and ideologies, inspiring humanity to overcome adversity and strive for a brighter future. Demissie, the senior consultant at Ethiopia's Policy Studies Institute, said the success of the Long March contributed directly to the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. In his view, the independent and modern state that emerged from that history has since become an important force in promoting multipolarity, South-South cooperation and the rise of the Global South. The Long March is not only a towering monument in the development of the Chinese nation, but also a precious spiritual asset for all humanity in the pursuit of independence, freedom and liberation, said Etienne, the Burundian sinologist. "Seen from the broader perspective of the Global South, the Long March proves a compelling point: to achieve genuine liberation and prosperity, a country and its people must proceed from their own conditions, uphold independence and self-reliance, and defeat every obstacle through unity and struggle," he said. Dennis Munene, executive director of the China-Africa Center at the Africa Policy Institute, said the Long March spirit could encourage the international community to unite around common goals and pursue dialogue across civilizations to address conflicts, climate change and poverty. These challenges cannot be resolved overnight; they require sustained commitment, cooperation and a willingness to keep working despite setbacks, he added. Kingdom, the research fellow at Uganda's Development Watch Center, said that writings by people like Edgar Snow about the Long March have moved people across the globe, "because every individual, wherever they are living, they usually have fears to conquer." "So, I feel like when you have examples of people who have gone the extra mile to conquer different things that are really relatable in some sense, it moves people," he said.
